channel.title: Parkers Physics — Field Notes
channel.description: Space weather event post-mortems, hindcast write-ups and simulation methods. What was forecast, what actually arrived, and where our own models diverged.

item.title: NOAA said G1. Earth got G3. The variable the models can't see.
item.description: On July 4, 2026 a geomagnetic storm arrived two full levels above forecast and put aurora over more than thirty states. Solar wind speed was unremarkable — Bz hit −19 nT and held southward for hours. Operational CME models carry no internal flux rope, so they cannot forecast the one variable that decided the outcome.

item.title: The index that lied: replaying the Gannon superstorm with a ring current
item.description: The May 2024 G5 pinned the planetary Ap index at its 400 ceiling for roughly a day while the magnetosphere kept going. A coupled BATS-R-US + Ridley + RCM replay measured Ap* = 524 past the clamp and cut storm-time density error 48% against GRACE-FO and Swarm-C truth.

item.title: The storm every model takes
item.description: St. Patrick's Day 2015 is the benchmark event for magnetospheric models. Here is how ours does on the two-step main phase.
